title: Mirror-conditioned learned optimizer
hypothesis: A shared learned coordinate update schedule conditioned on a compact domain Mirror code reaches at least 10% lower fresh query NRMSE than one unconditioned learned schedule and matches separately learned per-domain schedules within 5%, while using fewer optimizer-policy bytes than storing separate schedules.
physical_object: one shared 2D linear model and common update network/schedule basis
mirror_coordinate: one-bit domain Mirror code selecting/composing coordinatewise update rates
controls: two separate learned schedules (per-domain upper reference)
one shared learned schedule conditioned by domain Mirror code

task.type: 2D linear regression with two support-example covariance families

success_gate: Every fresh world and domain: conditioned schedule NRMSE <= 0.90x unconditioned learned schedule and <=1.05x separate per-domain schedule; N=20 serialized optimizer policy bytes are lower than two separate schedules.
failure_gate: Any quality or byte gate miss, or a direct domain-specific scalar learning-rate control matches conditioned policy.
boundaries: Domain identity is paid as a Mirror code and is known at inference.
No natural task or independent-capacity claim.

amendments.reason: Initial fresh payloads serialized only effective conditioned schedule, omitting shared base/modulation basis. Reconstruct and serialize both learned basis tensors plus domain code in each conditioned package. This is accounting-only; no task, model, quality, optimizer, or hyperparameter change; fresh errors remain unchanged.
